title: Linear projective actions, fixed subfunctors and rational tangent weight bases
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field], $G,T,S$ group schemes over $F$ [def-sc-group-scheme], and use their internal scheme actions, the actual character and cocharacter morphisms and multiplicative coordinate evaluation [def-sfb-rank-one-root-interfaces]. For $i:S\to G$, an action $a:G\times_F X\to X$, an $F$-algebra $A$ and $x\in X(A)$, define $\operatorname{IsFixed}(i,a,x)$ to mean that for every $F$-algebra map $A\to A'$ and every $s\in S(A')$ one has $a(i(s),x_{A'})=x_{A'}$. Let $P_n=\operatorname{Proj}F[X_0,\ldots,X_n]$ with its existing structure map [def-sfb-diagonal-projective-action]. For a rational representation $\rho:G\to\operatorname{GL}_{n+1}$ [def-sc-general-linear-group], an internal action $a$ on $P_n$ is its linear projective action on lines when for every test algebra $A$ and $g\in G(A)$ it is induced by the coefficient-fixing graded substitution $X_i\mapsto\sum_j\rho(g)_{ij}X_j$. Precisely this substitution and scalar inclusion have graded lifts with the irrelevant-ideal conditions for Proj maps, and the isomorphism $\operatorname{Proj}A[X]\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A\times_F P_n$ has the standard first projection and Proj of the inclusion as second projection; its composite with the restricted action is Proj of the substitution. For $i:T\to G$, an action on $X$, a rational point $e\in X(F)$ and a set $R$ of characters of $T$, define $\operatorname{HasTangentWeightBasis}(i,a,e,R)$ to mean: there are $x\in X$ and an isomorphism $\epsilon:\kappa(x)\simeq F$ inducing exactly $e$, and a $\kappa(x)$-basis $(b_\chi)_{\chi\in R}$ of the existing tangent space [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space], such that for every $t\in T(F)$ postcomposition of each dual-number vector $b_\chi$ with translation by $i(t)$ equals $\epsilon^{-1}(\chi(t))b_\chi$. For split tori over algebraically closed fields this is precisely a tangent character basis, including the empty basis. All definitions use the actual scheme morphisms and include nonreduced and zero test algebras.
